chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalty (hadd) of the Jew, the Christian, and the owned slave regarding wine and fabrication (of evidence) is the same. And indeed, the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Zimma) were reconciled upon the condition that they drink it in their houses.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّة: People of the Covenant (non-Muslim subjects under Islamic rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for wine consumption for Jews and Christians in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the legal penalty (hadd) for wine consumption applies equally to Ahl al-Zimma as it does to Muslims, reflecting the principle of uniformity in penal law. It highlights the specific condition of their covenant (sulh), which permits private consumption within their homes, thereby distinguishing their status from a total prohibition while maintaining the validity of the hadd upon public violation or specific legal circumstances.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Heasws said: ‘The Penalty of the Jew, and the Christian, and the owned (slaves) regarding the wine and the fabrication is the same. But rather, it is correct for the Ahl Al-Zimma (people under responsibility) that they can drink it in their houses’.
